diagnosis.hosted_failure: Root 44049970156 (88cd3091f) projection_bootstrap: psycopg DeadlockDetected on trade_journey_projection.event_receipts (oid 17073, ~4.1 GB, ~1.06M rows)
diagnosis.cause: bootstrap_schema runs every non-CONCURRENTLY migration in one transaction each deploy. 001 ran CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_event_receipts_ingested_seq (rebuild when absent, ShareLock on the table) and 002_drop_redundant_event_receipts_index then DROPped it (AccessExclusiveLock) while live projector writers queued on the same table. Additionally a bare CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS takes ShareLock on the table before noticing the index exists, which blocks writers even when nothing is built.
diagnosis.fix: 001 no longer creates idx_event_receipts_ingested_seq (event_receipts_ingested_seq_key UNIQUE already indexes it); 001's idx_event_receipts_tenant_env_journey creation is guarded by to_regclass in a DO block so an existing index takes no table lock; 002 drop retained (no-op without table lock when absent; one-time drop bounded by migration lock_timeout on legacy DBs).

rollback_cost.scenario: Roll back to a release whose 001 still creates idx_event_receipts_ingested_seq, then bootstrap on a DB where it was dropped
rollback_cost.measured_local: postgres:16 container, 1.06M rows, 223 MB table (padding is TOASTed): CREATE INDEX 0.36 s, index 23 MB, DROP INDEX 5 ms. Not hosted hardware.
rollback_cost.hosted_estimate: NOT MEASURED on hosted. Build reads the whole 4.1 GB heap; assuming 100-200 MB/s sequential IO this is roughly 20-60 s, plus sort of 1.06M keys (sub-second). Throughout, a ShareLock is held on event_receipts, blocking all projector INSERT/UPDATE for that duration, and the old 002 then needs AccessExclusiveLock behind them. Needs the old 002 to be bounded by migration lock_timeout, or operators should DROP the index CONCURRENTLY after rollback.
